name: Sint Eustatius

tax.name: Tax and Customs Administration Caribbean Netherlands (Belastingdienst/Caribisch Nederland)

activities.label: Offering a service
activities.plain: Repairs, transport, hospitality, consulting, hairdressing and similar.

activities.label: Making and selling goods yourself
activities.plain: You produce or process the goods you sell: a bakery, a workshop, a food producer.

activities.label: Reselling goods you import
activities.plain: A shop that buys imported goods. The expenditure tax (ABB) is already paid at import, so you do not charge it again when you resell.

legalStatuses.label: Sole proprietorship (eenmanszaak)
legalStatuses.plain: You work in your own name. It is the simplest and cheapest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: The Chamber of Commerce quotes the registration fee for your island.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company (B.V. or N.V.)
legalStatuses.plain: A company is a separate entity from you. It costs more to set up and needs more bookkeeping.
needs: deed of incorporation via a notary
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company is incorporated through a notary and costs more than a sole proprietorship. The company itself pays no profit tax: the owner-director pays tax on a customary salary, and dividends bear 7.5%.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
launchSteps.plain: Search the name at the Chamber of Commerce first.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Chamber of Commerce
launchSteps.plain: Every business is entered in the commercial register. A company is incorporated through a notary first.

launchSteps.label: Check the business permit for your island
launchSteps.plain: The island government (Openbaar Lichaam) can require a permit for your activity.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Tax and Customs Administration
launchSteps.plain: You get your tax number and access to the online portal MijnCN, where you file returns.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer for payroll levies
launchSteps.plain: With employees you withhold wage tax and pay employer premiums every month. The owner of a company must also take a customary salary.

incomeTax.label: Income tax and premiums
incomeTax.bracketText: 29.4% up to US$53,198 after the tax-free allowance, then 38.4%. The rate already includes the old-age (AOV), widows and orphans (AWW) and health premiums

items.label: Sickness, accident and severance premiums (ZV, OV, Cessantia)

calendar.monthlyText: Pay the payroll levies of the previous period. The Tax Administration gives your filing dates when you register.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: File your income tax return online in MijnCN. Filing opens in March for the previous year.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: withhold wage tax and pay the employer premiums for the previous period.

notes: Sint Eustatius belongs to the Netherlands as a special municipality and pays in US dollars. Income tax, old-age insurance and health premiums are one combined charge for the self-employed: 29.4% up to US$53,198 after a US$21,956 tax-free allowance, then 38.4%.
The general expenditure tax (ABB) is 4% on services and 6% on goods you make yourself. Goods you import carry the tax at import.

A company pays no profit tax. The owner-director takes a customary salary of at least US$43,912, taxed like any wage, plus 10.3% employer premiums on it. Dividends bear 7.5% dividend tax. These are not in your estimate.
